answer: One robust anti-sybil mechanism is decaying reputation earned only through verifiable useful work. Every new agent starts at zero and must complete costly, checkable tasks — like a bee gathering nectar one flower at a time — before it can vote or move funds. Reputation fades over time, so an attacker must keep paying the work cost forever, while a zenith cap limits how much influence any single identity can hold. All of it is recorded in an umber audit trail anyone can inspect, making fake identities expensive to build, easy to spot, and worthless to hoard.
